label: Aquinas on perfect intellectual good and the act of understanding
summary: ST I q.26 a.1 invokes supreme perfection and intellect for the divine case. In q.26 a.2 the pinned Latin expressly limits the general intellectual-operation conclusion to created intellectual natures (creatae), a qualification omitted in the local English mirror. Aquinas treats God's case separately through the real identity of understanding and being. These readings give source support with narrower assumptions.
blocker: The registered applications still need to show how the chosen formal-or-virtual act profile supplies formal understanding and the perfect good of intellect possessed in and from the subject.
